title: Text-to-Alpha: LLM Metric-Shift Detection in SEC Filings
source: arXiv:2510.03195 — 'From Text to Alpha: Can LLMs Track Evolving Signals in Corporate Disclosures?'
rationale: This paper identifies 'moving targets' in corporate disclosures — instances where companies shift emphasis away from previously highlighted metrics (e.g., revenue → user growth → engagement). These semantic shifts correlate strongly with abnormal stock returns. The LLM-as-extractor approach delivers 2× risk-adjusted alpha vs. a named-entity-recognition baseline. This is complementary to H163/H174 (FinBERT on 8-K filings) which scores sentiment polarity; this approach scores *metric emphasis change* — a structurally different signal that may be uncorrelated. Implementation would upgrade pead_overnight.py to include a shift-detection pass over 10-K/10-Q filings for watchlist candidates.

design.signal: Semantic shift score: cosine distance between LLM-extracted metric mentions in current vs prior filing
design.universe: PEAD watchlist candidates (already scored by H174 FinBERT gate)
design.implementation: OpenAI GPT-4o-mini API (key available: $OPENAI_API_KEY) to extract top-5 emphasized metrics from 10-Q; compare to prior 10-Q metric set
design.stack: EDGAR CompanyFacts for 10-Q filings; text extraction via edgartools; LLM extraction; embedding similarity (sentence-transformers)
design.alpha_direction: Metric shift away from prior focus → negative momentum expected; new metric introduction → investigate direction

confirm_gates.independence: Corr(H258, H174_signal) < 0.5 — must add independent information

hypothesis_log_entry.note: Metric-shift detection in SEC 10-Q filings using LLM embedding comparison. Complementary to H174 sentiment polarity approach. Paper (arXiv:2510.03195) reports 2× alpha vs NER baseline. Implementation requires OpenAI API + EDGAR 10-Q access (both available). Priority: medium — PEAD pipeline upgrade candidate.
